own_solution.law: Parallel resistors share the applied voltage: P = V^2(1/R1 + 1/R2). Thus P = 12^2(1/6 + 1/12) = 36 W. A series-aiding cell changes this to P = (12 + q)^2/4.
assumptions: Battery internal resistance and wire resistance are negligible.
The fan operates in a separate electrical circuit.
The fuse is initially intact and has negligible resistance while conducting.

T15AD.regime: The fuse remains intact when the branch current V/R1 = 2 A is below its rating q; all listed ratings satisfy 2 A < q.

T30BD.regime: The fuse remains intact when the branch current V/R1 = 2 A is below its opening threshold q; all listed thresholds satisfy 2 A < q.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TC44B and TA887 omit the number and unit required by the general instruction for same-quantity variants, although the authors explicitly identify these sentences as deliberate numeral-free controls.

notes: All physics claims and certified answers check out. For added emfs of 1.5, 3 and 4 V, the powers are respectively 45.5625, 56.25 and 64 W. Disconnected additions leave 36 W unchanged. The fuse branch carries 2 A, below every listed rating; opening that branch leaves 12 W in the second resistor, as claimed. Both explicitly designated numbered minimal pairs match in number and unit. I downgrade the pass-1 rendering flag from high to medium: pass 2 establishes that the missing numerals are intentional controls, with no false claim that those controls preserve the numbered minimal pair. Their departure from the general rendering instruction does not make the physics or an authors' claim wrong.
